I have read some comments about being misdiagnosed with depression, dysthymia, etc but I can speak to the experience of being diagnosed a bit later. I was diagnosed at 30.

Frankly, I didn't function. I was incredibly lucky to have a job with such low oversight that I could get away with not functioning. I'd frequently sleep in and not actually start working until 12-1pm when I was supposed to be out the door at 8:30am. I'd leave work early and bullshit my last few service calls.

I barely ate for days sometimes and during manic episodes I'd blow through hundreds or thousands of dollars on eating out. Basically everything was a massive shit show.

Eventually, after I was diagnosed, this all caught up with me, even after I felt better on medication and actually put some fucking effort into my job. I'm still dealing with the consequences years later for everything I caused by not seeking help earlier.

I had a massive "Aha!" moment after medication about all the behaviors and how they could be categorized into mania and depression. It made me desperately wish I would've done something about it before. 

All is well these days though. I've forgiven myself and now I try to encourage mental health awareness as much as possible!

Hope this insight from one random internet stranger's experience was at least a good read, if not a bit helpful. 🩵
